title: Kinematics
short_title: displacement, velocity, acceleration and motion graphs
standard_text: Motion can be described with displacement, velocity and acceleration: uniform and accelerated motion, motion graphs, the kinematics equations, free fall, and vectors. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Physics 11)
meta_desc: Free Physics 11 worksheets (BC Curriculum): displacement, velocity, acceleration and motion graphs. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: On a velocity–time graph, the slope is acceleration and the area is displacement.
body_html:
How to think about it

Displacement is change in position with a direction; velocity is displacement ÷ time; acceleration is the change in velocity ÷ time. On a position–time graph the slope is velocity; on a velocity–time graph the slope is acceleration and the area is displacement.

For constant acceleration: v = u + at, d = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2ad. In free fall a = 9.8 m/s² downward. Vectors add tip to tail; perpendicular vectors combine with the Pythagorean theorem.

Example

A car goes from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 4.0 s. What is its acceleration?

a = Δv ÷ Δt

Answer: 5.0 m/s²

Example

You walk 3 m east then 4 m north. What is your displacement?

Pythagoras

Answer: 5 m (about 53° north of east)

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up distance and displacement.
  • Using the slope of a position–time graph as acceleration.
  • Forgetting the sign of g.

faq.q: Can an object be accelerating at zero velocity?
faq.a: Yes: a ball at the top of its throw has v = 0 but a = 9.8 m/s² down.
